name: LTX-2.3 Fast
description: LTX-2.3 Fast is a performance-optimized variant of LTX 2.3 designed for rapid video generation with synchronized audio. It supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and audio-conditioned workflows while prioritizing speed, responsiveness, and cost efficiency for draft, preview, and high-velocity creative production use cases.
rules: Width and height must be sent together.

model.description: Identifier of the model to use for generation.

taskType.description: Identifier for the type of task being performed

taskUUID.description: UUID v4 identifier for tracking tasks and matching async responses. Must be unique per task.

positivePrompt.description: Text prompt describing elements to include in the generated output.

width.description: Width of the generated media in pixels.

height.description: Height of the generated media in pixels.

duration.description: Length of the generated video in seconds. The total number of frames produced is determined by duration multiplied by the model's frame rate (fps).

fps.description: Frames per second for video generation. Higher values create smoother motion but require more processing time.

seed.description: Random seed for reproducible generation. When not provided, a random seed is generated in the unsigned 32-bit range.

numberResults.description: Number of results to generate. Each result uses a different seed, producing variations of the same parameters.

lora.description: With LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation), you can adapt a model to specific styles or features by emphasizing particular aspects of the data. This technique enhances the quality and relevance of generated content and can be especially useful when the output needs to adhere to a specific artistic style or follow particular guidelines.

weight.description: Strength of the LoRA influence. A value of 0 means no influence. Higher values increase the influence, and negative values can be used to steer away from the LoRA's style.

oneOf.description: Apply LoRA only to the high-noise processing stage (coarse structure and early generation steps).
Apply LoRA only to the low-noise processing stage (fine details and later generation steps).
Apply LoRA to both stages for full coverage.

transformer.description: Transformer stages to apply LoRA. Some video models use separate high-noise and low-noise processing stages, and LoRAs can be selectively applied to optimize their effectiveness.

enhancePrompt.description: Enable automatic prompt enhancement for cinematic results.

inputs.description: The unified payload wrapper for complex media assets dictating image, video or audio inference constraints.

frameImages.description: An array of frame-specific image inputs to guide video generation. Each item can be either a plain image input (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64) or an object that pairs an image with a target position in the video. Must include at least one image that is not the last frame.

anyOf.description: Image input (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

image.description: Image input (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

oneOf.description: Zero-based frame index. Use -1 for the last frame.

frame.description: Target frame position for the image. Accepts a named position like `first` or `last`, or a zero-based frame index (-1 for the last frame).

audio.description: Audio input (UUID or URL). Enables audio-to-video conditioning. The audio is merged with the generated video and trimmed to fit the video duration. Maximum duration 30 seconds.

safety.description: Content safety checking configuration for video generation.

checkContent.description: Enable or disable content safety checking. Increases total generation time.

mode.description: Safety checking mode for video generation.

webhookURL.description: Specifies a webhook URL where JSON responses will be sent via HTTP POST when generation tasks complete. For batch requests with multiple results, each completed item triggers a separate webhook call as it becomes available.

includeCost.description: Include task cost in the response.

uploadEndpoint.description: Specifies a URL where the generated content will be automatically uploaded using the HTTP PUT method. The raw binary data of the media file is sent directly as the request body. For secure uploads to cloud storage, use presigned URLs that include temporary authentication credentials.

ttl.description: Time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for generated content. Only applies when `outputType` is `URL`.

outputFormat.description: Specifies the file format of the generated output. The available values depend on the task type and the specific model's capabilities.

outputQuality.description: Compression quality of the output. Higher values preserve quality but increase file size.

oneOf.description: Returns an immediate acknowledgment with the task UUID. Poll for results using getResponse. Required for long-running tasks like video generation.

deliveryMethod.description: Determines how the API delivers task results.
